portion_doctrine: Unreal Engine 5 world-building and game mechanics video transcript. Segments 21-30 cover Megascan asset workflows, nanite geometry, foliage painting, and Blueprint game scripting (character ragdoll, obstacles, collision events, UI widgets). This is pure tool tutorial content with no strategic/business value. Extraction focuses on actionable mechanics, parameter names, and workflow steps.
operating_rules: Megascan parameters for 3D props: Albedo Tint (color), Albedo Controls (saturation, brightness, contrast, all default 1.0), Metallic (override base metallic), Roughness (max 1.0), Normal Strength (controls normal map intensity)

Material parameter naming: In Unreal, duplicate parameter names are treated as the same within material instances. Rename each parameter uniquely (e.g., 'size_grass' vs 'size_dirt') to control independently

Foliage parameters: Color Overlay (tint), Color Variation (range 0.05-0.1 for realism), Roughness Intensity (0=shiny, 1=default), Normal Intensity (0=no normal maps), Translucency Strength (default 7.0, light bounce), Translucency Desaturation (0.95 default), Enable Grass Wind (with intensity 0.05-0.15 range for subtle movement)

Nanite geometry: Enables near-infinite source polygons on screen. Only works for solid static meshes (not foliage/deformable). Enable via right-click > Nanite > Enabled. Nanite Quality downloads 8K textures + highest poly density. Performance gains: 5-10 FPS to 40-60 FPS in test (100K donut models)

Blueprint event firing: Right-click to add nodes; connect outputs to inputs via drag. Keyboard events available (F key fires event). Nodes can be organized with reroute nodes (hover wire, double-click). Shortcuts: Ctrl+B jump to asset location, Ctrl+E open static mesh editor, Alt+2 wireframe view

Custom events in blueprints: Create custom events (right-click > Custom Event) to expose functionality between blueprints. Example: Third-person character 'Death' event callable from obstacle blueprint via cast

Ragdoll implementation: 3-node sequence: (1) Set Collision Enabled (Collision Enabled Query and Physics), (2) Set Simulate Physics (enabled), (3) Set Physics Blend Weight (0 to 1). Connect all to single mesh reference to stay organized

Foliage painting density: Density default 0.5. In foliage editor, can set density value up to 500+. Scale range for variety (example: 0.5 to 2.0 random scale X). All foliage types can be bulk selected with Ctrl+A

LOD (Level of Detail): Visual transition as camera distance changes. LOD0 (closest), LOD1, LOD2, LOD3, LOD4 (billboard farthest). Billboard materials must match main material edits (e.g., color tint) or visible pop-in occurs. Edit both independently

Blueprint variables: Create via Variables panel + icon. Types: Boolean (default), Float (decimal numbers). Must compile before editable. Expose via Instance Editable + Expose on Spawn checkboxes in details. Exposes in level editor instance properties

Delta time frame-independence: Use Delta Seconds output from Event Tick to multiply rotation/movement. Example: Make Rotator node with X = Delta Seconds * 100, ensures same speed regardless of frame rate

Collision volumes for gameplay: Capsule Collision larger than visual geometry (else character collides with mesh before collision volume). Use On Component Begin Overlap event. Cast to specific character class to filter valid overlaps

Level blueprints: Right-click selected actor in level editor > Add Event for [ActorType] > Collision > Add On Actor Begin Overlap. Level blueprint events trigger on map-specific logic (win conditions, UI popups)
Widget UI creation: Canvas (window container) + Text element. Anchoring to center of screen keeps UI centered regardless of resolution. Details panel controls text content, font size, appearance

Foliage variation techniques: scale randomization, color variation ranges, translucency controls for plant realism

contradictions: LOD performance optimization: stated as 'no longer needed with Nanite' but Nanite generates automatic LOD anyway; unclear if manual LOD still required when Nanite enabled
Foliage support: video states 'Nanite doesn't work for foliage yet' but also says Epic is working on it; unclear current status as of session date
weird_gold: Unreal smart-names physics: Setting Collision Enabled as 'Collision Enabled Query and Physics' (not just 'Enabled') required for ragdoll blend weight to work; parameter name matters to engine behavior

Billboard pop-in mitigation: If you edit main foliage material (e.g., color tint), you MUST edit the billboard material separately, or visible pop-in occurs at distance. Foliage has two independent materials
Frame-rate stress-test command: backtick key opens console; 't.MaxFPS 30' locks framerate, reveals frame-dependent bugs. Essential debugging tool for physics/movement
Quixel Bridge quality is file-size aggressive: 8K nanite quality creates massive project files; 4K recommended unless final render output. No in-engine quality switcher for runtime LOD
